why: U1 is the R-785.0 5V DC-DC module (not a logic IC) with its own internal input/output capacitors; C7 is the extra 100nF on its +5V output, 13.4 mm centre-to-centre (9.2 mm pad-to-pad), acceptable for a bulk-rail cap. Marginal, not a defect.

Record irlz44npbf-to220ab names the JEDEC package TO-220AB; KiCad calls the same package TO-220-3_Vertical. The pads and the 3-pin pinout are crosschecked (PR-PAD/PR-SYM pass); only the name string differs. package is a signed field, so renaming it means re-running the crosscheck - P1 follow-up, not a board defect.

Record k7805-2000r3-module describes the part ('SIP-3 DC-DC module (R-78 style)'); the footprint is KiCad's Converter_DCDC_RECOM_R-78B-2.0_THT, whose 3 pads at 2.54 mm / 1.20 mm drill were checked against the YLPTEC datasheet. package is a signed field - re-sign in a P1 follow-up. Not a board defect.

KiCad's Isolator:PC817 has EMPTY pin names on all four pins, so the registry names (A, K, E, C) cannot be matched by name. Pin numbers and geometry agree with the datasheet (1 anode, 2 cathode, 3 emitter, 4 collector); the record stays unverified until the owner signs it (see its notes). U2 is connected BY FUNCTION in netlist.py, so a wrong pinout cannot hide behind this waiver.

P1-T9b: first time the parts stage sees the reflex fixture. KiCad TO-220-3_Vertical drills 1.10 mm, the LCSC/EasyEDA footprint 1.30 mm. The 1.10 mm drill fits the datasheet maximum lead diagonal (1.08 mm) with 0.02 mm to spare (lint PR-HOLE WARN, accepted in spec decision 9.10); the board is hand-soldered. A human should decide whether to enlarge the hole to 1.2 mm before ordering.
P1-T9b: KiCad drills 1.20 mm = the YLPTEC datasheet's recommended-layout hole (p5), LCSC's EasyEDA footprint uses 1.00 mm. KiCad matches the datasheet; not a board defect.

P1-T9b: DIP-4 / DIP-16 drills are 0.80 mm in KiCad vs 1.00 mm in the LCSC footprint. DIP leads are ~0.25-0.5 mm thick, 0.80 mm is the KiCad standard and fits with margin; the LCSC hole is just looser. Libraries legitimately differ.
